query: What three sub-models constitute the VIPVLIB simulation model chain proposed by Samadi et al. (Doc 3)?
ground_truth_answer: 1) Optical Model, 2) Thermal Model, and 3) Electrical Model.

expected_claims.claim_text: The VIPVLIB simulation model chain comprises three distinct models: 1) An Optical Model (calculates dynamic solar irradiance accounting for position and curvature), 2) a Thermal Model (predicts PV cell temperature factoring in vehicle speed and wind cooling), and 3) an Electrical Model (computes I-V characteristics and net energy yield).
expected_claims.verbatim_quote: The VIPVLIB simulation model chain comprises three distinct models: 1) An Optical Model (calculates dynamic solar irradiance accounting for position and curvature), 2) a Thermal Model (predicts PV cell temperature factoring in vehicle speed and wind cooling), and 3) an Electrical Model (computes I-V characteristics and net energy yield).

query: According to Barabas et al. (Doc 4), what physical trade-off occurs when retrofitting roof-mounted PV modules?
ground_truth_answer: Added surface roughness increases aerodynamic drag (Cd), increasing road load consumption that counteracts solar power generation.

expected_claims.claim_text: added surface roughness and altered boundary layer profile increase aerodynamic drag coefficient (Cd) and frontal area, increasing mechanical road load tractive consumption, which must be offset by solar electrical generation
expected_claims.verbatim_quote: added surface roughness and altered boundary layer profile increase aerodynamic drag coefficient (Cd) and frontal area, increasing mechanical road load tractive consumption, which must be offset by solar electrical generation

query: Combining Doc 2 (MPPT buck converter) and Doc 3 (Thermal Model): How does vehicle velocity influence net electrical generation efficiency?
ground_truth_answer: Higher vehicle speed increases forced convective cooling, lowering module operating temperature and mitigating thermal efficiency loss.

expected_claims.claim_text: Increasing vehicle speed increases forced convective cooling over the PV modules, lowering operating temperature and mitigating thermal efficiency degradation during operation.
expected_claims.verbatim_quote: Increasing vehicle speed increases forced convective cooling over the PV modules, lowering operating temperature and mitigating thermal efficiency degradation during operation.

query: In Doc 2, what control strategy determines whether solar power charges the traction pack or auxiliary battery?
ground_truth_answer: A Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) monitoring the state of charge (SoC) of both battery packs.

expected_claims.claim_text: A Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) monitors the state of charge (SoC) of both battery packs and dynamically routes solar power to maximize overall vehicle operational efficiency.
expected_claims.verbatim_quote: A Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) monitors the state of charge (SoC) of both battery packs and dynamically routes solar power to maximize overall vehicle operational efficiency.

query: In Doc 3, how does relative air velocity affect PV module temperature compared to stationary PV?
ground_truth_answer: Relative velocity (v_rel = v_veh + v_wind) increases convective heat transfer coefficient (h_conv), lowering module temperature.

expected_claims.claim_text: Relative velocity (v_rel = v_veh + v_wind) increases the convective heat transfer coefficient (h_conv), significantly lowering module equilibrium temperature compared to stationary PV installations.
expected_claims.verbatim_quote: Relative velocity (v_rel = v_veh + v_wind) increases the convective heat transfer coefficient (h_conv), significantly lowering module equilibrium temperature compared to stationary PV installations.

query: At high cruising speeds (100–130 km/h in Doc 4), does a roof-mounted PV array produce a net energy surplus or deficit?
ground_truth_answer: Net energy deficit: Aerodynamic drag penalty exceeds the 200–350 W generated by the roof solar panel.

expected_claims.claim_text: at high cruising speeds (100-130 km/h), the aerodynamic drag penalty consumes more electrical energy than the roof PV array can generate (~200-350 W), resulting in a net energy deficit compared to a clean aerodynamic roofline.
expected_claims.verbatim_quote: at high cruising speeds (100-130 km/h), the aerodynamic drag penalty consumes more electrical energy than the roof PV array can generate (~200-350 W), resulting in a net energy deficit compared to a clean aerodynamic roofline.

query: Why do standard stationary PV testing conditions (STC: 1000 W/m^2, 25 deg C) misestimate real VIPV yields according to Docs 1 & 3?

expected_claims.claim_text: Transient shading and non-planar 3D curved surfaces cause stationary STC ratings to misestimate VIPV output by 20% to 40%.
